import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 633

*Reference:*
* [erdosproblems.com/633](https://www.erdosproblems.com/633)
* [So09] Soifer, Alexander, How Does One Cut a Triangle? I
* [So09c] Soifer, Alexander, Is there anything beyond the solution?
-/

open Affine
open scoped Congruent EuclideanGeometry Similar

namespace Erdos633
variable {n : ℕ} {T : Triangle ℝ ℝ²}

variable (n T) in
/-- A triangle is `n`-cuttable if it can be decomposed into `n` congruent triangles. -/
def IsCuttable : Prop :=
  ∃ Ts : Fin n → Triangle ℝ ℝ²,
    (∀ i j, (Ts i).points ≅ (Ts j).points) ∧
      Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (Ts i).interior (Ts j).interior) ∧
      ⋃ i, (Ts i).closedInterior = T.closedInterior

/-- A triangle isn't cuttable into zero triangles. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 51]
lemma IsCuttable.ne_zero (hT : IsCuttable n T) : n ≠ 0 := by
  rintro rfl
  obtain ⟨Ts, -, -, hT⟩ := hT
  exact T.closedInterior_nonempty.ne_empty <| by simpa using hT.symm

/-- Every triangle is cuttable into any non-zero square number of congruent triangles. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 51]
protected lemma IsCuttable.sq (hn : n ≠ 0) : IsCuttable (n ^ 2) T := sorry

/-- Every triangle is cuttable into any non-zero square number of congruent triangles. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 51]
lemma IsCuttable.of_isSquare (hn₀ : n ≠ 0) (hn : IsSquare n) : IsCuttable n T := by
  obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := hn; rw [← sq]; exact .sq <| by simpa using hn₀

/-- A triangle whose side lengths and angles are integrally independent is cuttable only into
a non-zero square number of congruent triangles. This is proved in [So09c]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 51]
lemma isCuttable_iff_isSquare_of_linearIndependent
    (hTsides : LinearIndependent ℤ
      ![dist (T.points 0) (T.points 1),
        dist (T.points 1) (T.points 2),
        dist (T.points 2) (T.points 0)])
    (hTangles : LinearIndependent ℤ
      ![∠ (T.points 0) (T.points 1) (T.points 2),
        ∠ (T.points 1) (T.points 2) (T.points 0),
        ∠ (T.points 2) (T.points 0) (T.points 1)]) :
    IsCuttable n T ↔ n ≠ 0 ∧ IsSquare n := by
  exact ⟨fun hT ↦ ⟨hT.ne_zero, sorry⟩, fun hn ↦ .of_isSquare hn.1 hn.2⟩

/-- Which triangles can only be decomposed into a square number of congruent triangles? -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51]
lemma erdos_633 : T ∈ (answer(sorry) : Set <| Triangle ℝ ℝ²) ↔
    ∀ n, IsCuttable n T → IsSquare n := sorry

variable (n T) in
/-- A triangle is `n`-simili-cuttable if it can be decomposed into `n` similar triangles. -/
def IsSimiliCuttable (n : ℕ) (T : Triangle ℝ ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ Ts : Fin n → Triangle ℝ ℝ²,
    (∀ i j, (Ts i).points ∼ (Ts j).points) ∧
      Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (Ts i).interior (Ts j).interior) ∧
      ⋃ i, (Ts i).closedInterior = T.closedInterior

/-- A triangle isn't simili-cuttable into zero triangles. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 51]
lemma IsSimiliCuttable.ne_zero (hT : IsSimiliCuttable n T) : n ≠ 0 := by
  rintro rfl
  obtain ⟨Ts, -, -, hT⟩ := hT
  exact T.closedInterior_nonempty.ne_empty <| by simpa using hT.symm

/-- Every triangle is simili-cuttable into any number of similar triangles, except 0, 2, 3, 5.
This is proved in [So09]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 51]
lemma IsSimiliCuttable.of_ne_zero_two_three_five (hn₀ : n ≠ 0) (hn₂ : n ≠ 2) (hn₃ : n ≠ 3)
    (hn₅ : n ≠ 5) : IsSimiliCuttable n T := sorry

/-- There exists a triangle which isn't simili-cuttable into 0, 2, 3, 5 parts.
This is proved in [So09]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 51]
lemma exists_isSimiliCuttable_iff_ne_zero_two_three_five :
    ∃ T, ∀ n, IsSimiliCuttable n T ↔ n ≠ 0 ∧ n ≠ 2 ∧ n ≠ 3 ∧ n ≠ 5 := sorry

end Erdos633

findings.description: The docstring attributes the square-only result to [So09c]. The appropriate reference is [So09b], “How Does One Cut a Triangle? II,” pp. 37–39. [So09c], Problem 6.4 on pp. 47–48, instead discusses uniqueness of the standard subdivision into k² congruent triangles under these independence hypotheses. The Lean assertion itself agrees with the result reported on the Erdős page; this is only a citation-location issue.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/633 attributes the square-only result to [So09b], adding that it holds whenever the sides and angles are both integrally independent. Soifer’s Chapter 4, pp. 37–38, develops the nonsquare-count obstruction using integral independence and the eigenvalue √n. In Chapter 6, Problem 6.4 says that “the only way to cut T into k² triangles congruent to each other is the way presented in Figure 2.2.” Public previews: https://page-one.springer.com/pdf/preview/10.1007/978-0-387-74652-4_4 and https://page-one.springer.com/pdf/preview/10.1007/978-0-387-74652-4_6.
findings.suggested_fix: Add [So09b] to the bibliography and cite it in this lemma’s docstring. Retain [So09c] as the reference for the original classification question. No mathematical statement change is needed.

status_issues.recorded: @[category research open], with an unknown Set-valued answer.
status_issues.source_status: The source now marks the classification problem SOLVED. Beeson, Laczkovich, and Zhang give a complete classification in arXiv:2604.03609, first submitted 4 April 2026; the current version is v3, dated 25 August 2026.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/633 states: “A complete classification is given by Beeson, Laczokovich, and Zhang [BLZ26].” The paper’s abstract says it settles Problem 633, and Theorem 1 gives eight cases characterizing triangles admitting a nonsquare tiling. See https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.03609.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to `research solved` and add [BLZ26]. When supplying the explicit answer, retain its Set-of-triangles type and use the complement of the nonsquare-tilable classes in Theorem 1, rather than a Boolean answer.

reformulations.difference: The source uses geometric, unlabelled triangles, whereas Lean requires congruence of the ordered vertex families, with corresponding indices agreeing for every pair of tiles.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a nonempty dissection, choose a reference tile and independently relabel every other tile to match it. Transitivity of congruence gives the required common vertex correspondence. Reindexing a simplex preserves its interior and closed interior, so disjointness and coverage are unchanged. Conversely, ordered congruence implies geometric congruence. I proved the equivalence with a formulation explicitly allowing a vertex permutation for each pair of tiles; the proof also handles n = 0.

reformulations.difference: As with congruent dissections, Lean uses ordered vertex families rather than similarity up to a vertex permutation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Relabel each tile to match a fixed reference tile. Symmetry and transitivity of similarity then establish similarity with common corresponding indices for every pair. The relabelling preserves both interior sets used in the dissection conditions. The converse is immediate. The permutation-explicit formulation and the file’s definition were proved equivalent in Lean, without using any admitted problem theorem.

review.notes: Checked all ten declarations and their underlying definitions. Lean experiments in /workspace/review/boundaries.lean, reindex.lean, domain.lean, and inspect_clean.lean compile. They confirm impossibility of zero-piece dissections, existence of one-piece dissections, nonemptiness of the triangle domain and triangle interiors, and that disjoint interiors prevent duplicate tiles. The Set-valued answer correctly constrains the classification, and the exact exceptional-count formulation is equivalent to the source’s counterexample assertion together with its universal similarity theorem. No mathematical misformalization was found. The reviewed file was not modified.
